acceptanceCriteria: The system displays the promo code discount amount for both the outbound and return trip line items in the Mozio email confirmation when a promo code is applied to a return trip order.

The system calculates the promo code discount amount for the return trip line item using the same logic applied to the outbound trip line item, ensuring both legs reflect the correct discounted total.

The Mozio email confirmation renders the promo code amount in the same format and position for the return trip as it does for the outbound trip (e.g., line-item-level discount line showing the promo code label and amount).

When a return trip order contains multiple line items with different fromStation/toStation pairs (e.g., AJ→UN and UN→AJ), the system applies and displays the promo code discount for each line item independently.

When a promo code applies only to the outbound leg and not the return leg (per promo code configuration), the system does not display a promo discount amount for the return trip line item, and the email confirmation reflects this without error.

When the promo code discount amount is zero or the promo code is not applicable to the return trip, the system either omits the promo discount line for the return trip or displays a zero-amount entry consistently with how zero-discount outbound legs are handled.

The system includes the promo code discount amount for return trip line items in the order payload data that feeds the Mozio email confirmation template, matching the structure used for outbound trip line items.

The system correctly handles return trip orders where dateFrom and dateTo span different calendar dates (e.g., 2026-02-25 to 2026-03-05) and still displays the promo code discount amount for both legs in the email confirmation.

notes: Reviewed openspec's 8 ACs. Modified 3, flagged 0, added 5 new criteria. AC2 (original) said 'calculated using the same logic' which is vague and untestable — replaced with a specific observable outcome: the net total for the return trip equals base fare minus discount, matching the outbound calculation pattern. AC6 (original) had an either/or ('omits…or displays a zero-amount entry') which is ambiguous for testing — resolved to 'omits' to match the more common email pattern and remove ambiguity; if the system should display zero instead, that needs explicit product decision. AC7 (original) referenced internal 'data structure' which borders on implementation detail — refined to focus on the observable outcome (data is present and accessible to the template enabling correct rendering). Added 5 new ACs: (1) no-promo-code baseline scenario, (2) promo code expired for return date but valid for outbound, (3) decimal/currency formatting consistency, (4) edge case where discount exceeds base fare, (5) accessibility of promo discount text in the email.
